title: NaN is not equal to itself
why_it_matters: Checking for NaN the wrong way never works.
explanation: NaN means 'not a number', and it's the one value that isn't equal to itself, so === can't detect it. Use Number.isNaN(value). It returns true only for the real NaN, unlike the old global isNaN, which converts its input first.
code:
console.log(NaN === NaN);                 // false
console.log(Number.isNaN(NaN));           // true
console.log(Number.isNaN("abc"));         // false
console.log(Number.isNaN(Number("abc"))); // true
try_it: Quiz: what is 'abc' * 2? Run it, then test the result with Number.isNaN.
